questions.q: Name the four main ministers who advised the Mughal Emperor at the centre.
questions.a: The four ministers are the Vakil (prime minister), Diwan (finance), Mir Bakshi (military), and Khan-i-Saman (household). A wrong answer suggests the student is confusing Mughal administration with modern democratic roles or misremembering the specific terminology of the era.

questions.q: Why did the Mughal Emperor need a council of ministers if he had "absolute authority"?
questions.a: Absolute authority means the Emperor had the final say, but the empire was too large for one person to track every detail of finance and military records personally. A wrong answer shows the student believes "absolute power" means doing every job alone, missing the concept of delegation.

questions.q: If the Emperor wanted to know if the army had enough resources for the year, which minister would he consult?
questions.a: He would consult the Mir Bakshi (military minister) for troop needs and the Diwan (finance minister) for the budget. If the student answers incorrectly, they haven't grasped the functional division of labor in the administration.

questions.q: How did the Mughal administrative system differ from earlier systems like the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.a: The Mughal system refined and expanded upon the Delhi Sultanate’s model by adding more specialized roles and a more sophisticated structure. An incorrect answer suggests the student thinks the Mughals invented everything from scratch, ignoring the historical evolution mentioned in the text.

questions.q: Is it more efficient for an Emperor to control every single decision or to delegate tasks to ministers? Why?
questions.a: Delegation is more efficient because ministers become experts in their specific fields, allowing the Emperor to focus on major policy decisions. A wrong answer indicates a misunderstanding of how complex systems (like an empire or even a large company) scale up their operations.

questions.q: If you were the Emperor, which of the four ministerial positions would you find most challenging to manage and why?
questions.a: A good answer identifies a minister (like the Mir Bakshi or Diwan) and explains that their role involves high-stakes resources (money or weapons) which are prone to corruption or error. A poor answer is vague or fails to justify the choice with the duties assigned to that minister.
